weaknesses: Mechanism engagement is now proven, but C1 still fails because benign activations are dragged along the harmful direction by 0.156, above the 0.10 gate
Current signed-cos objective has no stopping condition, so it keeps driving harmful cos to -1.0 even after the pass threshold is reached, wasting capacity and increasing spillover
Retention weighting is presently too weak relative to the aggressive RR term, as evidenced by perfect harmful anti-alignment alongside systematic benign drift at every site
The reproducible tail-step instability remains present (step-490 grad spike and retention blow-up), so final-step checkpoints are unreliable even if best-checkpoint behavior is acceptable
Because harmful reroute overshot the target by a large margin, this run does not yet demonstrate controlled selective rerouting, only maximal inversion

code_diffs: Add a new RR loss option `signed_hinge`.
Implement it as L_rr = mean(max(cos(a_site, d_site) + m, 0)) over harmful examples/sites, where `m` is provided by `--rr_margin` and set to 0.3 for this run.
Interpretation: optimization stops pushing once cosine reaches -0.30, matching the actual success threshold instead of driving toward -1.0.
Keep all other objective terms unchanged to isolate saturation of the reroute term as the single causal change.
Retain per-site train and held-out cosine logging every 25 steps for both harmful and benign examples.
Shorten training from 500 to 400 steps to avoid the known collapse tail; select/report best checkpoint by held-out C1-composite rather than final step.

rationale: Iteration 1 validated my prior diagnosis: the loss, not capacity, was the blocker. But the new failure is the mirror image: pure signed cosine has constant incentive to keep pushing after the gate is already passed, so the adapter spends excess freedom driving harmful residuals to -1 and drags benign residuals with it. The cleanest one-iteration fix is therefore to saturate the RR objective at the actual target boundary, not to globally weaken it. A hinge at margin 0.3 preserves the strong O(1) gradient near cos≈0 that successfully engaged the mechanism, but turns that gradient off once the required reroute level is achieved. That directly targets the observed pathology—overshoot-induced benign bleed—without introducing a confound from rebalancing multiple coefficients. I am also accepting a 400-step cap because the step-490 collapse is already replicated and contributes no useful evidence. If this works, we should see harmful held around the pass region while benign drift drops under the gate.
expected_signal: Held-out M4 should show Δcos(a_h, d_h) in roughly [-0.45, -0.30] with per-site harmful cos near the margin rather than -0.99, Δcos(a_h, d_ctrl) remaining ~0, and Δcos(a_b, d_h) improving from -0.156 to within [-0.10, 0.00]. C1 should pass on both harmful and benign sides at the best checkpoint, with no reliance on the unstable final steps.
still_unresolved_after_fix: Tail-step training instability remains only partially addressed unless the shorter run fully avoids it
